title: SSO & Role Controls: Pricing Differentiation and Contract Commitment Matrix
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Define a clear pricing and contract commitment model for SSO (SAML / IdP integrations) and RBAC such that enterprise customers can choose between: self-serve add-on, SLA-backed configuration, or contractual commitments with indemnified security obligations. Deliver required contract language, pricing tiers, and product gating rules for the console and onboarding flows.
background: Sales and Solutions Engineering report long procurement cycles due to ambiguous SSO / RBAC commitments. Current internal offers are inconsistently documented across account teams; legal frequently rewrites SSO clauses during negotiation. This causes both lost deals and mismatched expectations post-sale. We need a repeatable packaging model that maps product behavior (self-serve vs committed) to contract language and pricing.
proposed_solution: Create three offering tiers for SSO/RBAC: Free/Self-serve (standard), Managed-Config (paid add-on), Contracted-Assurance (contract commitment with SLA & remediation obligations)
Define product gating: console UI flags for 'Managed-Config' enablement, API flags and onboarding checklist for contract-signed 'Contracted-Assurance' customers
Draft modular contract clauses (legal template) for each tier: responsibilities, timelines for SSO provisioning, breach notification, and RBAC auditability commitments
Set clear pricing: one-time setup fee for Managed-Config, recurring premium for Contracted-Assurance. Publish estimate grid for Sales to use during quoting
Implement a simple entitlement model in the Console and in the billing backend to enforce gating and surface billing line items
Coordinate engineering tickets for SSO onboarding workflow, RBAC exportable policies, audit logs retention options, and support SLAs
acceptance_criteria: Legal provides modular clause templates for all three tiers and approves playbook language
Sales enablement deck and quoting spreadsheet published and used by at least 3 AE teams in pilot
Console UI shows entitlement flags for Managed-Config and Contracted-Assurance and corresponding onboarding checklist
Billing events emitted for Managed-Config setup and Contracted-Assurance monthly premium
Pilot contract signed by two customers using Contracted-Assurance with no redlines to SSO clauses in >75% of cases
Metrics pipeline tracks time-to-provision SSO for each tier and shows a measurable improvement vs current baseline
rollout_plan: Week 1: Finalize pricing bands and legal templates; get executive approval
Week 2: Implement entitlement flags in Console (feature-flagged), update billing events; prepare AE playbook
Week 3-4: Run 4-week pilot with 2 enterprise deals via Solutions Eng; collect negotiation feedback
Week 5: Iterate contract language; update onboarding workflow; ramp to all AE teams
Post-launch: Monitor sign-up friction, provisioning time, and support escalations for 8 weeks and iterate
metrics: Negotiation time (days) on contracts with SSO clauses
Percent of deals that accept Contracted-Assurance without redlines
Number of support escalations related to RBAC in first 90 days
ARR uplift attributable to Managed-Config and Contracted-Assurance line items
risks: Overly prescriptive contract language may increase legal negotiation time for some customers
Engineering scope creep if RBAC audit/export requirements expand mid-project
Incorrect billing implementation could mis-bill enterprise customers and cause revenue leakage
If entitlement gating is poorly communicated, customers may have poor provisioning experience leading to churn
notes: We intentionally separate Managed-Config (operational service) from Contracted-Assurance (legal SLA) to avoid blurring support and contractual obligations
Consider optional add-on: SOC2 gap remediation assessment for Contracted-Assurance customers at premium
Recommend a customer-facing doc set: onboarding checklist, expected timelines, and admin guide for SSO / RBAC
Eng must expose an API hook for sales ops to mark accounts as Contracted-Assurance post-signature
